title: DevExp: Novice Onramp Observations and Quickstart Gaps
content:
Meeting: DevExp quick weekly - focused on novice onramp (45m)
Date: 2026-09-17
Attendees: Sofia (owner), Ethan, Priya, Liam, 2 UX testers (recorded), + notes from support triage
Minutes taker: Sofia

Purpose: capture real-user friction observed in last two quickstart runs (internal bootcamp + external new signups), summarize reproducible gaps, and assign surgical fixes / docs patches. Not a big redesign; scope is triage + 1-week fixes where possible.

Agenda:
- 0-5m: quick recap of scope and metrics (drop-off, time-to-hello)
- 5-20m: live playback of two bottlenecks (SDK auth + sample app env)
- 20-35m: brainstorm minimal fixes + owner mapping
- 35-45m: priorities and next steps, put on board

Quick metrics snapshot (from onboarding inhaler metrics, Sept 10-16):
- median time-to-first-successful-call: 14m (goal: <5m)
- 37% of new trials abandoned before running sample app
- 18% error rate on first HTTP sample call (mostly 401s, CORS, and outdated examples)
- top feedback: confusing API key placement, unclear CORS guidance, mismatched package names between README and pip/npm registry

Observed friction (concrete examples):
1) Auth confusion: sample README shows export REDWOOD_API_KEY=..., but cloud quickstart sends new users to a sidebar token UI labeled "client secret". People try the browser token in server-side example (401).
   - Reproduction: fresh sandbox acct -> follow quickstart -> copy token from client UI -> run server-sample server.js -> 401 (logs show token_type=client)
   - Notes: UX testers described "which token do I use for node?"; support tickets reference the same wording.

2) SDK package mismatch & package manager instructions outdated
   - README: uses `@redwood/inference` but npm shows `@redwood-inference/sdk` in registry; pip wheel name changed last month. New users copied the wrong install command and hit import errors.
   - Example error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood_inference'

3) CORS + browser sample landing page tries to use embedded API call from client without guidance about CORS proxies for hosted accounts (old quickstarts assumed server-for-everything).
   - Result: browser console shows CORS preflight blocked; users open tickets asking why front-end tutorial fails.

4) Sample app env var mismatch & fast-fail messages not actionable
   - Missing or badly worded error messages (e.g., "auth failed"). Need clear remediation lines: check key origin (client vs server), check region, check example package version.

Proposed low-cost fixes (prioritized):
A. Short-term (this week) - docs + sample edits (owners: Priya / Ethan)
   - Update quickstart README to show explicit token types with copy/paste examples: server token vs client token; small diagram 2 lines. (PRI: HIGH)
   - Patch npm/pip install commands to match current registry names; add a single verification step `node -e \"require('@redwood-inference/sdk'); console.log('ok')\"` or equivalent for python. (PRI: HIGH)
   - Add explicit CORS note with two recommended patterns: (1) server-side proxy snippet (2) link to our hosted CORS guide). (PRI: MED)
   - Improve error message text in sample server to catch client-token-in-server-error and print remediation. (owner Ethan)
B. Medium-term (2-4 weeks) - sample app changes + CI checks (owners: Liam / Eng infra)
   - Add a quick local smoke test in samples repo that runs a minimal invocation and checks for 200 vs 401; run on PRs for quickstarts. (PRI: MED)
   - Add a small gating test in releases that confirms package names in README match package registry. (PRI: MED)
C. Nice-to-have (Q4) - onboarding UX changes (owner: product/ux)
   - Revamp token UI labels to indicate "server token (for backend)" vs "client token (for browser)" and a tooltip explaining security implications. (tie-in with CONFLUENCE:DEVEXP/Onramp-Playbook)

Decisions made in meeting:
- We will not change server token behavior this sprint. Focus is documentation + sample fixes.
- Any code change that could inadvertently log secrets is blocked until SRE review. Create a short checklist.

Action items (owner - due):
- Priya: Draft README quickstart patch with explicit token section + one-liner diag (due 2026-09-20). Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples-repo/pull/458 (WIP).
- Ethan: Add client-token detection in server sample and change thrown error text to actionable remediation (due 2026-09-22). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devexp-sdk/pull/412 (draft).
- Liam: Prototype a minimal smoke test and CI job for quickstarts; get infra approval for running 1 ephemeral request per PR (due 2026-09-24).
- Sofia: Collate support tickets with same error strings and add to shared board (JIRA:RI-2345) + update Confluence Onramp doc to reflect these fixes (due 2026-09-21).
- UX: Product/UX to scope label changes for token UI (meeting next Tue). (product owns)

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we add an explicit "Quickstart checklist" in repo that we require before merge? (pros/cons: slows merges vs reduces churn).
- Are we okay with CI smoke tests hitting hosted API in PRs? Need rate/cost estimate; Liam to run numbers.
- How to communicate to existing users when we rename packages or change install commands (release notes vs automatic redirect).

Notes to self / loose ideas (unresolved):
- Could generate a single one-file runbook that prints the exact commands for Node/Python/Ruby with token placement examples (copyable). Might reduce support volume.
- Consider adding an endpoint in the SDK that returns "token_type" or a hint (cannot return secret) to help detect common mistakes client/server. Requires design review.

UX tester quick quotes:
- "I was unsure whether to paste the token into terminal or browser console."
- "The install command failing felt like the tutorial was broken."

Support snippets to reuse in docs (for quick copy):
- "If you get 401: confirm you are using a server token for backend examples. If you copied the token from the client-side panel in the console, create a server token in Account > API Keys. See step X."
- "If the import fails: verify the npm package name matches this install line: npm i @redwood-inference/sdk"

Risks and guardrails:
- Any quickstart server patch must not log keys. Add test to run node sample and assert no console.log contains 'key' or 'secret' in CI. (Ethan to add).

Next check-in: quick sync on Friday 2026-09-18 (10m) to confirm PRs opened and smoke test feasibility.

Attachments / references: brief video clip of UX run (internal link in slack thread), list of ticket excerpts (JIRA RI-2345), draft PR links above.

End of notes.

-- Sofia
